sections.markdown:
## C — Driving habits, turns, bicycles and motorcycles

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A22
A safe driver knows and respects the rules, follows proper procedures, keeps a good attitude and is courteous at all times, using good habits on every trip, short or long. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A22
On entering the car, adjust the seat and mirrors, make sure passengers are seated so they will not interfere, and buckle up with every passenger before switching on the ignition. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A22
With a manual transmission push in the clutch before turning the key; with an automatic, have the indicator in park or neutral and press the brake as you turn the key. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A22
Sit upright and grip the outside rim with both hands, firm enough for control but not so tight it slows your reflexes, removing a hand only to signal or operate the vehicle. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A22
To leave a parallel parking space, look over your shoulder and in the mirrors, wait until clear, signal, and enter the nearest lane, staying there until a lane change is safe. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A22
You must keep within a single lane, never weaving between lanes or straddling the lane marking. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A23
A traffic lane is any part of a road wide enough for a vehicle or line of vehicles to travel safely, and it exists whether or not it is marked. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A23
Plan each turn early rather than at the last moment, and move into the proper turn lane well before it once the change is safe. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A23
Signal at least 100 feet before turning and keep the signal on until you actually turn, so both pedestrians and drivers know your intention. [A23]
Why it matters: signaling only as you start to turn is a common mistake; the signal must come well before the turn.
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A23
Both hands belong on the wheel during the turn itself, and pedestrians have the right of way over motor vehicles. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A23
Slow down before turning, check front, rear and sides for cars and pedestrians, finish in the proper lane, and cancel the signal afterward. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A23
In daylight you may add hand and arm signals to your signal lights, because bright sunlight can make a flashing signal hard to see. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A23
For a right turn from a four-lane or divided highway, get into the right lane well ahead and turn tightly into the right lane of the cross street. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A23
For a left turn there, move to the lane nearest the center line or divider, turn from the inside lane without a wide swing, and enter just right of the cross street's center line, unless signs or markings allow turns from more lanes. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A25
A three-point turn reverses your direction and must not endanger other traffic, so it is normally allowed only where you can be seen from far away and traffic makes it safe. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A25
Three-point turns are banned on interstate freeways, on curves, and near hilltops where drivers approaching within 500 feet from either direction cannot see you. [A25]
Why it matters: the ban applies even where no sign is posted, because local ordinances govern these turns.
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A25
Local ordinances govern three-point turns, there may be no warning signs, and prohibiting signs are usually posted only at hazardous spots. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F18 | anchor: A25
Slow down before a curve so you do not cross the center line or leave the road, entering slowly enough to accelerate slightly while rounding it. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F19 | anchor: A25
People on bicycles have the same road rights and responsibilities as people in motor vehicles, so drivers and cyclists alike must know and obey state traffic laws. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F20 | anchor: A25
A cyclist on a roadway rides as close as practicable to the right curb or edge, except when passing, preparing a left turn, or avoiding hazards such as debris, opening car doors or pedestrians. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F21 | anchor: A25
People on bicycles may ride two abreast at all times, and they must ride with the flow of traffic. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F22 | anchor: A26
Cyclists signal turns, lane changes and stops with the same hand and arm signals that drivers use. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F23 | anchor: A26
Cyclists must use a bicycle lane where one exists; sidewalks and multipurpose paths are not bicycle lanes, and riding a bicycle on the sidewalk is illegal in Alabama. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F24 | anchor: A26
Cyclists under 16 must wear a securely fastened helmet on public roads, other public rights-of-way, public bicycle paths and in public parks. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F25 | anchor: A26
A driver may enter a bicycle lane only to park where parking is allowed, to enter or leave the highway, or to prepare for a turn. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F26 | anchor: A26
To turn across a bicycle lane, move into the lane before the turn, but only when doing so does not endanger a cyclist using it. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F27 | anchor: A26
Alabama law requires at least three feet between your vehicle and a person on a bicycle when you pass, and wind from fast vehicles can push a cyclist enough to cause a crash. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F28 | anchor: A26
Avoid passing a cyclist uphill, on curves, where visibility is limited, or when other vehicles occupy the lane you would need to use. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F29 | anchor: A26
When a narrow road makes passing unsafe, stay a safe distance behind the cyclist, without tailgating or blasting the horn, until you can pass. [A26]
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F30 | anchor: A26
Watch closely for cyclists at intersections, when crossing sidewalks, and when entering or leaving alleys or driveways [A26] [A27].
Source: [A26 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F31 | anchor: A27
A bicycle brakes far less well in wet weather, so drivers should allow for its reduced ability to slow or stop. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F32 | anchor: A27
State law says bicycles should carry lights or reflectors for night riding, and drivers need extra caution in darkness or poor visibility. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F33 | anchor: A27
Motorcyclists share the same road rights and responsibilities as other users, and a substantial share of motorcycle crashes involve riders with limited experience. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F34 | anchor: A27
A motorcycle is only about two feet wide against a car's five to six feet, so it is hard to pick out and its distance and speed are hard to judge. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F35 | anchor: A27
Left turns in front of an oncoming motorcycle cause a large share of car-motorcycle injury crashes, so look twice and know the motorcycle's speed before you turn left. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F36 | anchor: A28
Before turning in front of any vehicle, make sure it is really turning and not going straight with a forgotten signal still blinking. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F37 | anchor: A28
Leave the same 2-second following distance behind a motorcycle as behind any vehicle, since tailgating can distract the rider. [A28]
Why it matters: a smaller vehicle does not mean a shorter gap; the following distance stays the same.
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F38 | anchor: A28
A motorcycle is entitled to a full lane, and a driver must never pull alongside it in the same lane, even a wide one, which is illegal and very dangerous. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F39 | anchor: A28
Give motorcycles even more following distance in darkness, rain or on wet, slippery roads, and watch for rain glare that can hide a rider at night. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F40 | anchor: A28
Crosswinds on open highways and bridges, windblasts from fast large trucks, and road hazards such as gravel, seams, manhole covers, rough rail crossings or metal bridges can make a rider suddenly change speed or direction. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0028]

Glossary: traffic lane — road width enough for safe travel, marked or not [A23]. Bicycle lane — road space striped, signed and marked for cyclists, never a sidewalk or multipurpose path [A26]. Three-point turn — turning around to face the opposite direction [A25].
Memory aid: for motorcycles, look twice before a left turn, and never share their lane [A27].
